newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish stock values up 23 percent so far in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Danish stock values up 23 percent so far in 1996.

text.p: The Danish stock exchange all-share index has risen by 23 percent in 1996 to date and is expected to continue upward for the rest of the year, an analysis by the Berlingske Tidende daily said on Monday.

It said that the combined market value of listed shares rose from 386 billion crowns at the end of 1995 to 477 billion at the close of business last Friday and was expected to swell by another five billion by December 31, 1996.
The best-performing sector, the paper said, was shipping, with an average 37 percent rise. The lowest returns came from insurance shares, which gained a modest five percent.
Much of the gain came during the third quarter of 1996, during which time the KFX top 20 index gained nine points - or 13 percent.
October has been another boom month, with the index hitting closing highs on eight out of 14 trading days so far.
Although bank shares have repeatedly been cited as among the most popular of late, the banking sector rose on average only 12 percent over the survey period.
